newsitem.title: USA: HP says Q1 workstation sales on track.
newsitem.headline: HP says Q1 workstation sales on track.

text.p: A senior executive heading Hewlett-Packard Co's Unix systems business said sales in the segment are on track after the lead month of the company's first fiscal quarter of its 1997 financial year.

"We're still on track," Dick Watts, vice president and general manager of HP's Computer Systems Organization, which is responsible for the company's higher-end, Unix-based businesses, told Reuters in an interview.
Wall Street has been concerned over recent weak sales of workstations despite product upgrades in the summer, although it posted higher orders for servers in its October quarter.

"We did have a strong finish in workstations," he said of the pickup in workstation sales in October, the final month of the company's fiscal year, after weakness in August and September despite introductions of fast new machines.
Watts said the biggest reason for the slow acceptance of the new Unix workstations was due to lack of availability of applications ported to the new products.

Analysts have said HP's weakness in workstations follows a general industry trend, but note that rivals Sun Microsystems Inc seem to have made market share inroads by launching their own upgraded products earlier in the year.
Customer appraisals of the Microsoft Corp's latest Windows NT operating system, version 4.0, released in the summer, may also have resulted in some lost business, according to industry analysts.

Watts said evidence from competitive losses in the Unix business so far had not demonstrated any significant shift to Windows NT, while adding that "The NT encroachement is still difficult to measure yet in terms of lost deals."
A possible larger factor is deals that have been held up pending evaluation of NT or other features, he said.
"There is a bit of a holdback," Watts added.
Watts said HP has been working with its major applications suppliers to ensure their programs will run on it latest Unix products, and has been winning recent benchmark trials.
By the end of the company's first fiscal quarter at the end of January, major applications should be available for use on its new higher-end products, Watts said.

The executive said HP expects if anything to increase its investments in the Unix arena in the near term, saying it expects it can improve on its 16 percent overall share of the total workstation and server market.

The mainframe market continues to offer opportunities for machines like Hewlett-Packard's as applications which used to run on mainframe computers are shifted to cheaper, high performance workstations and servers, he said.
